Kallosemjen Jewish Cemetery 2

Jewish Cemetery · Kállósemjén, Hungary

Demolished. The second of two Jewish cemeteries in Kállósemjén, also appearing on an 1872 cadastral map but completely demolished, presumably during WWII. It served the same community as the village's other cemetery: settled in the mid-18th century, declared Orthodox in 1869, and subordinated to the Nagykálló Jewish community from 1885. By 1944, the Orthodox community numbered 107; on April 22 that year, 94 Jews were confined by Hungarian gendarmes before deportation via the Nyíregyháza Ghetto to Auschwitz. 21 survivors returned; by 1949, only 6 Jews remained.
